coherent structures, such as subsidence and updrafts, are the main contributors to the vertical mass and heat fluxes in the cloud layer, while downdrafts and shells dominate the downward transport in the trade inversion.
updrafts, subsiding shells, and environmental subsiding are the most frequent and significant contributors to the vertical mass transport in the boundary and the cloud layer of shallow convection.

updrafts are the most frequent and important contributors to the vertical heat and moisture transport in the boundary layer, while downdrafts and shells are the most important transporters in the trade inversion and the cloud layers.

the role of coherent structures, such as the updrafts, subsiding shells and environmental subsidence, in the boundary layer and the cloud layers of the shallow cumulus.
understanding the role of coherent structures on vertical transport of heat, moisture, and momentum in the boundary layer and cloud layer.
the fate of coherent structures in the boundary layer and the cloud layer, and how they affect the transport and entrainment of heat and moisture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the boundary layer updrafts, shells, and subsidence are the most frequent and dominate contributors to the vertical mass, heat, and moisture transports in the shallow cumulus cloud system.
updrafts, subsiding shells and environmental subsidence are the dominant contributors to the transport of heat and humidity in the boundary and the cloud layers.

the vertical mass, heat and moisture flux in the boundary and shallow cloud layer is dominated by updrafts and subsiding shells, with a lesser but still important role of the environmental subsidence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

updrafts are the main contributor to vertical transport of heat, moisture, and momentum in the cloud layer and the trade inversion layer, while the environmental subsidence is the main contributor to the vertical transport in the boundary layer and the free troposphere above the trade inversion layer.

the boundary layer is a dynamic system that is constantly being fed by updrafts and shells and is constantly losing mass to subsidence, and that the boundary layer has a significant influence on the cloud layer, which is not only fed by updraft mass but also receives significant heat and moisture transport from the boundary layer.

coherent structures, such as downdrafts and subsiding shells, are important contributors to the vertical mass and heat transport in shallow convection, while updrafts are the main contributors to the vertical moisture transport.
The main takeaway from our work is that
coherent structures are the dominant contributor to vertical mass and moisture transport, and thus should be the focus of entrainment and detrinement studies in shallow convection.

the boundary-layer subsidence and downdraft/shell structures are the main contributors to the vertical heat and moisture fluxes, and that environmental subsidence is not a significant contributor to the vertical transport in the cloud layer.
updrafts are the dominant transporters of moisture and heat in the cloud layer, whereas downdrafts are the dominant heat and moisture transporters in the cloud-free boundary layers.
